boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all seven frozen records in Jackson’s Valley Campaign. Preserve per-engagement dates, including Princeton’s May 15–17 interval and separate Cross Keys/Port Republic dates. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 12,300 total (US 8,500; CS 3,800). The live NPS field reads 12300 total (US 8500; CS 3800;).
claims.rationale: Source field only. Formations, engaged troops and changing concentrations do not establish matched opening populations. Live zeros are not measured absence; shared provenance is not independent corroboration.

claims.value: Allan places Jenks’s battery on a hill west of Kernstown.
claims.rationale: Attributed local position, not a verified map or inherited terrain advantage; deployment may be commander-created.

claims.rationale: No battle-specific supply, ammunition or transport return was inspected. Formation lists and retrospective descriptions are not readiness measures.

claims.value: The NPS narrative attributes Jackson’s advance to an estimate of about 3,000 Union troops; Allan describes information received through Ashby that understated the remaining force.
claims.rationale: Both are retrospective accounts. The original report, its delivery and Jackson’s exact knowledge were not inspected; agreement does not establish independent corroboration.

claims.value: Allan attributes the attack to a desire to recall Union troops leaving the Valley.
claims.rationale: Retrospective account of purpose, not a measured strategic benefit or an inspected original order. The recorded tactical defeat remains a Union victory.

claims.value: Allan identifies Kimball as the senior officer commanding on the field in Shields’s absence.
claims.rationale: Field command and divisional authority are different roles; neither receives automatic sole credit. The live heading calls Kimball brigadier general but the narrative and frozen listing call him colonel; the heading does not revise the frozen rank or establish a transfer clock.

claims.value: The same CWSAC/NPS record gives 3,800 Confederate troops in its force field but describes a 3,400-man division in its narrative.
claims.rationale: Retain the internal discrepancy without choosing a canonical figure or assuming equal population/timing. Imported numerical bounds remain unchanged.

claims.value: The frozen result remains Union victory.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,308 total (US 590; CS 718). The live NPS field reads 1308 total (US 590; CS 718;).
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Original orders, returns, casualty reconciliation, contemporary message chains and precise command clocks remain deferred after the bounded pass. No whole-book, facsimile or map verification is claimed.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Allan is one interested retrospective history where used. Embedded reports are not additional independently inspected families. Princeton retains only the frozen NPS/CWSAC family.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
